Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300.

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

This drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

Recent findings suggest that on Thursday, November 19, AI manufacturer Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

Sources indicate that with the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

Sources indicate that coinGlass data demonstrates $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

It has been revealed that according to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is at the moment trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Recent findings suggest that until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

It has been revealed that bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

  • Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.
  • After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (which we had the pleasure to see firsthand), Genesis launched the upcoming “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that genesis opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000. If you want coach doors, however, it will cost you a bit more.

Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.

After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (which we had the pleasure to see firsthand), Genesis launched the upcoming “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.

The Genesis GV90 introduces several “world-first” innovations, including the first independently opening and closing B-pillarless coach doors, a 12-airbag roof airbag system, and genuine wood floors with radiant heating.

It’s available in two models: the GV90 Standard with traditional swing doors and the GV90 Neolun, which features the “Neolun Arch Gate,” Genesis’ hidden B-pillar coach door system.

In Korea, the Genesis GV90 Standard 7-seater model starts at 139.5 million won, or about $104,000.

The GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) starts at 145.5 million won ($108,500); the GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) starts at 189.9 million won ($141,500), while the top-spec GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) starts at 239.5 million won ($178,500).

Based on Hyundai’s latest eMP platform, developed exclusively for its flagships, Genesis noted the GV90 is like a “moving private lounge,” complete with a multi-chamber air suspension and a dual electronic limited-slip differential (E-LSD).

The platform is designed to open up interior space for the B-pillarless coach doors, swivel seats, and more.

When parked, the front seats swivel a full 180 degrees to face rear passengers or to create what Genesis calls “a face-to-face lounge-like configuration.”.

The interior is about as over-the-top as you could expect, with massive digital screens, premium materials, and plenty of luxury extras.

The GV90 is the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle to feature its upcoming extendable display and the first Genesis model equipped with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.

Together, they create what Genesis calls a fresh realm of “display expandability.” While other vehicles, like the new Tucson and IONIQ 3, also use Pleos Connect, Hyundai developed an exclusive version for the GV90.

When the vehicle is parked, the screen can expand to 24.6″ at the push of a button, transforming it into a massive Cinematic Display.

Once extended, the display switches to Media Home mode, where you can watch Netflix, live TV, stream music, and more with third-party apps.

It has been revealed that A mobile private theater wouldn’t be complete without a premium audio system, right? To top it off, Genesis added a 25-speaker Bang & Olufsen Premier 3D Sound System with Dolby Atmos, so it sounds like you’re actually at the movies.

In place of a traditional instrument cluster, the GV90 has a 25″ Head-Up Display (HUD) that reveals the vehicle’s speed, navigation directions, and other ADAS functions directly on the windshield.

The GV90 is also the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle with a buttonless power system. When you enter the vehicle and close the door, the Motion Column Shifter moves from the 12 o’clock position to the 2 o’clock position.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the Crystal Sphere between the driver and passenger rotates to indicate it’s ready to drive. The vehicle starts when you press the brake.

As a full-size flagship SUV, the Genesis GV90 is massive. It measures 208.1″ (5,285 mm) long, 79.9″ (2,030 mm) wide, and 71.5″ (1,815 mm) tall (71.4″ with 24″ tires), with a 127.8″ (3,245 mm) wheelbase.

That’s even bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 (199.2″/5,060 mm in length) and Kia EV9 (197.4″/5,010 mm).

Recent findings suggest that to power a full-size flagship SUV, it needs a massive battery. The GV90 uses a 123.5 kWh battery, the largest among Hyundai Motor’s EVs, which Genesis said provides a driving range of 500 km (310 miles) for the 7-seater version with 22″ wheels.

The GV90 Neonlun 6-seater with 24″ wheels has a range of up to 460 km (286 miles) on a single charge.

It’s equipped with a newly introduced dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) system that delivers a combined 657 hp (490 kW) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque, making it Hyundai Motor Group’s most powerful electric vehicle.

When using a 350 kW fast charger, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.

According to recent reports, and.... once again Hyundai shortchanges the range. If you are going to drop a 200+ inch premium upright SUV into the market it requires a 140+ kwh battery (Rivian, BMW) to deliver segment appropriate range. You do not have to jump to a 200 kwh Escalade (though it is probably a better buy in every respect) but at least deliver 140+. Also, memo to powertrain engineering group: 350 kw is getting outdated on fast charging especially on a vehicle of this size. And while I am at it, what happened to the promised L3 ADAS? I think the 2028 Caddy is worth the wait compared to this.

“Thanks to the enthusiastic interest and support for the GV90 since its global premiere, we have begun full-scale sales in Korea first,” a Genesis official said, adding the flagship SUV will “set a new standard for luxury.”.

Following Korea, Genesis is expected to launch the GV90 in the US and other global markets in early 2027.

Recent findings suggest that genesis has yet to reveal US prices, but the GV90 Standard model is expected to start at around $100,000. The GV90 Neolun, on the other hand, will likely start closer to $150,000 or more.

Sources indicate that what do you think of the flagship Genesis GV90? Would you buy the standard version for about $100,000 or pay the extra for the Neolun with coach doors? Let us know in the comments.

Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
  • According to recent reports, A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) noted in a report published on Thursday.
  • "Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais mentioned in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.

According to recent reports, A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) noted in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais mentioned in a statement.

Industry observers note that the 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.

Sources indicate that IOSCO stated the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day.".

In a recent development, swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report remarked. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.

It has been revealed that because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO noted. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.

According to recent reports, wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has said. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.

The report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.

Layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report remarked.

Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has stated the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.

Sources indicate that IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to enhancement cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.

Industry observers note that most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.

No surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO said it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.

According to recent reports, quantum hardware is advancing quickly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has said it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

Despite continued weakness across the broader crypto market, Ethereum [ETH] is showing an interesting development on the staking front.

According to Santiment’s data, Lido Staked Ethereum (stETH) recorded net outflows of 4,186 tokens from exchanges, marking its largest single-day outflow since the 30th of May.

As a result, there has been a decline in the amount of stETH immediately available on exchanges for potential selling.

This comes as Ethereum was trading near $1,753.91 at press time, after a drop of 2.9% in the past 24 hours.

It has been revealed that at the same time, around 836,798 ETH is at the moment waiting to enter Ethereum’s validator network. Of this, the estimated waiting period currently stands at 14 days and 13 hours, with a processing rate (churn) of 256 ETH per epoch.

Meanwhile, the exit queue presents a different picture wherein around 164,005 ETH is waiting to leave the validator network, with an estimated waiting period of 3 days and 20 hours.

Looking at the broader picture, Ethereum right now has approximately 773,650 active validators, with 44.6 million ETH staked. This represents around 36.5% of Ethereum’s total supply, while the network’s annual percentage rate (APR) stands at 2.42%.

So now, if exchange outflows continue, the entry queue remains elevated, and ETH prices begin stabilizing, these developments could strengthen the argument that investors are positioning themselves for the longer term rather than preparing to sell into market weakness.

Interestingly, all of this coincided with a recent report by AMBCrypto where Ethereum’s staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high of 36.3%, with approximately 44.5 million ETH locked in staking, up from 42.1 million in mid-August.

Meanwhile, institutional players such as BitMine and SharpLink continue expanding their staking activities, with BitMine holding 5.22 million staked ETH and earning $121.4 million from staking and validation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia.

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Industry observers note that nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Debuted earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

That rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

It has been revealed that the issue also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

The TTWO spike indicates tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

It has been revealed that the seven-day moving average of mean inflow rose by 86.2%, pointing to a substantial increase in the average deposit size. The moving average reached about 1.72 billion SHIB per deposit. The latest unsmoothed mean inflow was roughly 2.76 billion SHIB per deposit.

It has been revealed that from a price perspective, the SHIB chart demonstrates a clearly bearish pattern, with the downtrend continuing rather than a recovery taking shape. Falling trading volume alongside the price could suggest that selling pressure is easing, but it should not be seen as a sign of a reversal.

Recent findings suggest that SHIB was trading at $0.00000370 on the Binance daily chart on November 20. The session low at the time of the snapshot was $0.00000365. The asset was below all the moving averages shown on the chart, and the RSI was near the oversold area. The brief bounce after the latest drop also stayed below $0.000004.

Industry observers note that for SHIB to make a lasting recovery, it needs to break above the $0.000004 price level. Price moves below this level are unlikely to provide a solid base for recovery.

Privacy and cybersecurity have become an vital part of the internet browsing experience in the current world. VPNs, or Virtual Private Networks, have grown in usage and in relevance over the years due to this.

However, not all VPNs offer the same level of performance, transparency, value, or protection as others; some are great for advanced privacy features, while others are better for streaming. Here is our list of the top picks for the month:.

According to recent reports, expressVPN aims to make online privacy secure and internet access straightforward for everyone. It is available on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android. Lightway is a proprietary VPN protocol designed to establish connections rapidly and reduce battery consumption while also improving reliability when switching between networks.

There are 3 subscription tiers on ExpressVPN: Basic, which has the core VPN protection and encrypted connections, along with essential privacy tools. Advanced, with additional security features and expanded protection tools, and password management options—lastly, Pro, a comprehensive package with additional privacy and identity-protection features.

According to recent reports, cyberGhost VPN focuses on accessible internet privacy and user-friendly VPN applications. It has specialised server categories that let users select servers that are optimized for streaming, downloading, and general browsing.

Sources indicate that the platform also has a no-logs policy, security features like AES-256 encryption, an automatic kill switch, split tunnelling, and DNS leak protection. CyberGhost is a great option for beginner-level people who want an easy-to-use app with specialized server choices.

Nord VPN is one of the most popular options on the market; it has grown over the years from a conventional VPN provider into a broader cybersecurity platform. The Plus plan has features like password management and threat protection, while the Complete plan has VPN protection with additional security and encrypted cloud-storage services.

NordLynx is a WireGuard-based VPN protocol that has been designed to deliver faster connections without having to compromise on privacy. There are also Double VPN, Onion Over VPN, split tunnelling, and an automatic kill switch.

Surfshark offers unlimited simultaneous device connections and has WireGuard, OpenVPN, AES-256 encryption, a kill switch, and MultiHop connections. There is an option to generate an alternative online identity and email address for users who do not want to share their details.

It has subscription prepares with varying rates and features. Industry observers note that proton VPN keeps user information safe without slowing them down or selling them out. It uses AES-256 and ChaCha20 encryption across various protocols and blocks ads, trackers and malware on paid plans.

Industry observers note that there are various subscription intends including a free, VPN Plus and a Proton Unlimited one. Proton VPN also supports WireGuard,   , Stealth and a kill switch. On the paid plans it blocks ads, trackers and malware along with support for split tunnelling.

It has been revealed that the MACE feature on PIA also helps to block ads, trackers and other malicious domains. Automation rules, port forwarding and encryption settings can all be customised by users on the platform.

It has been revealed that XRP has spent a week unable to get back above $1. In November 2026, the token hit a two-year low of $0.895, and on Nov. 20, it was trading near $0.96. XRP is down 27.7% in November and about 51% since January, according to CryptoRank data.

Recent findings suggest that the last time XRP lost more than 28% in a month was February 2025, when the token fell 29.3%. That month, the crypto market was also hit by a $1.5 billion hack of the Bybit exchange on Feb. 21.

Industry observers note that XRP did not recover right away. From March to June 2025, the token gained about 4.5% in total, according to CryptoRank. In July 2025, XRP jumped 35%, and on July 18, 2025, it set its all-time high of $3.65. On the same day, U.S. President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act, the country's first stablecoin law. XRP is now 73% below that record.

In November 2021, XRP lost 10%, and it fell another 17% in December and 25.6% in January 2022. In November 2022, the month of the FTX collapse, the token dropped 11.8%, and it lost 16.9% in December. XRP finished 2022 down about 59% and gained 20.1% in January 2023.

According to CryptoRank, XRP's median return is -10.2% in November and -4.07% in December.

In a recent development, soSoValue data indicates spot XRP ETFs have lost about $26 million to outflows since the start of November. About $19.1 million of that amount left the funds in the week ending Nov. 13.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 19, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said on CNBC that investors had been selling crypto to buy shares in substantial listings. "People are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market, crypto included — Bitcoin, XRP — and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Anthropic IPO. Porsche CEO takes a shot at Tesla’s ‘flying’ Roadster stunt show

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (881 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla’s “flying” Roadster just took a hit from Porsche.
  • Recent findings suggest that both automakers revealed their next halo cars on the same day, October 15.
  • Tesla finally unveiled the next-gen Roadster last month, almost nine years after the 2017 prototype.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla’s “flying” Roadster just took a hit from Porsche. Speaking at a conference in Berlin today, CEO Michael Leiters said Porsche wants “to completely steer clear from any kind of effects and highlights,” according to Bloomberg.

Recent findings suggest that both automakers revealed their next halo cars on the same day, October 15. Tesla made a Roadster flip in mid-air. Porsche revealed the Mission S, and Leiters indicates the two cars aren’t even chasing the same customers.

Tesla finally unveiled the next-gen Roadster last month, almost nine years after the 2017 prototype. The main event was a car using compressed-air thrusters to launch off a ramp, rotate in the air, and come back down on its wheels.

According to recent reports, it was the payoff for months of hype. Musk spent most of the year promising a “flying” Roadster demo, and it slipped more than once. We reported in June that it had been pushed to August to make room for SpaceX thruster work.

It has been revealed that there are three versions. The Performance trim uses suction fans and claims 0-60 mph in under 1.6 seconds, the Thrust trim adds rear cold-gas thrusters for a claimed sub-0.9-second run, and the single-seat Rocket trim gets thrusters all around the car and isn’t approved for public roads. Tesla gave no price and no production date, just Musk’s “2028, actually.”.

In a recent development, porsche went the other way. Under the skin, the Mission S can take either a hybrid or a straight combustion powertrain. It’s a mid-engine car that sits above the 911 in the lineup, and well above it in price.

According to recent reports, leiters stated customer response has been “overwhelming” and that Porsche would rather show off real technical innovation than put on a show. If it reaches production, Ferrari is the obvious target, and Porsche hasn’t played in that segment since the 918 Spyder. Porsche is counting on a pricier, more exclusive lineup to rebuild its profits.

Not everyone in the supercar world agrees with Leiters. Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna rated Tesla’s Roadster launch “10 out of 10” last month.

Leiters has a point, even if Porsche pitching a gas and hybrid supercar as “technical innovation” in 2026 is a bit rich. But what bothers me more is who Tesla is aiming at.

Sources indicate that I’m concerned Tesla is starting to appeal to the lowest common denominator: people who watch a Roadster hop off a ramp and believe an actual flying car is coming. Musk pushed that idea himself. On Joe Rogan’s show, he called the upcoming demo “unforgettable” and said that if Peter Thiel wants a flying car, “we should be able to buy one.”.

That’s not real. Cold-gas thrusters work like a giant can of compressed air, and the math is brutal. The Rocket trim carries 400 liters of air at 10,000 psi, roughly 200 kg of gas. At the roughly 80 kN its rear thrusters produce, even a very efficient nozzle empties that tank in a few seconds. Then refilling it takes six to seven hours.

According to recent reports, also someone on Bluesky pointed out that the video highlights Mach diamonds in the exhaust stream of the thrusters. Which means it's so loud that anyone within 100 feet would suffer immediate and permanent hearing loss. This Roadster isn't useful for anything other than temporarily pumping stock prices.

So the Roadster’s “flying” will always be limited to stunts like this one. No hopping over traffic. No hovering. A couple of seconds of air, then a long wait at a compressor.

That’s great for a viral clip. But this is a car that dropped from a promised 620 miles of range in 2017 to “over 300” today, and Tesla would rather sell people on a flight the physics can’t deliver.

According to recent reports, it’s hard for me to get excited for that. As a BEV enthusiast, I’m not more excited about Porsche’s ICE Mission S, but at least I trust Porsche to actually deliver that to customers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in New York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, over the past 17 months, the Wildlife Conservation Society’s Bronx Zoo in New York City has rescued dozens of parrots from the illegal pet trade. They include white-fronted Amazons (Amazona albifrons) and orange-fronted conures (Eupsittula canicularis).

According to recent reports, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) confiscated the orange-fronted conures during three separate operations over the last 17 months, and the white-fronted Amazons in the last several months. All of the birds were discovered at the U.S.–Mexico border.

“These animals were stolen from the wild and are victims of the illegal wildlife pet trade, and our responsibility is to give them the best possible chance for a healthy future,” Chuck Cerbini, WCS Bronx Zoo Curator of Ornithology, said in a statement. “Working with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, our veterinary and animal care teams provide specialized expertise to assess, treat, and care for confiscated wildlife.”.

When confiscated wildlife arrives at the Bronx Zoo, the veterinary and animal care teams first conduct a health check, provide any necessary medical treatment, and then help find long-term placements for those that can’t be released into the wild.

White-fronted Amazons are native to parts of Mexico and Central America and represent the smallest Amazon parrot. They are also one of the few parrot species in which males and females feature visibly different plumage. Both sexes have a white foreheads, red faces, and yellowish bills, but males have red shoulders and females have green shoulders.

In a recent development, orange-fronted conures, also known as half-moon conure or Petz’s conure, are also native to parts of Mexico and Central America, where they live in open woodlands, forest edges, and savannas. They have an orange forehead and green and blue feathers.

Recent findings suggest that the IUCN Red List categorizes both birds as a species of Least Concern, but that still  doesn’t justify trafficking them in the illegal pet trade. Parrots throughout Latin America are subject to both the loss of forest habitat and poaching.

Birds in particular l are especially threatened by trafficking because they are valued in the pet trade and the collector trade.

The XRP ETF market might be bracing to close a record-breaking month of outflows as demand for the XRP-based investment product has remained on hold all through the month.

This comes as the prolonged and intense market volatility has extended to the ETF ecosystem, causing institutional investors to withdraw their capital.

With November just about three weeks gone, the latest data from SoSoValue highlights that XRP ETFs have already recorded a total of $30.76 million in net outflows this November.

Previous ETF data shows that March remains the only month in which spot XRP ETFs have recorded net outflows since their launch.

While it still stands as the record outflow month for XRP ETFs, investors withdrew about $31.16 million from the funds during that month.

This means that the persistent withdrawals seen this month have brought the November outflow dangerously close to its previous monthly record seen in March.

Apparently, the spot XRP ETFs are on track to close November as their worst-performing month since launch, with just about $1 million left to hit the record.

Further data also highlights that the spot XRP ETFs have yet to record a single day of net inflows throughout November, as the persistent price decline has caused investors to slow down their purchases.

As such, the influx of fresh capital into the spot XRP ETF market has remained on hold amid growing market uncertainty and a shift in investor sentiment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase wants a piece of the prediction markets action, with the exchange reportedly planning a launch next year.

Right now, they don’t run their own; they borrow them. Users trade event contracts on the exchange through a Kalshi partnership. That could change next year though.

It has been revealed that citing sources close to the matter, a Bloomberg report claimed that Coinbase wants to roll out its own event contracts in the U.S in H1 2027. It would be open to both retail and institutional traders.

It has been revealed that but why bother? For starters, Coinbase gets to decide what launches and when. Next, it keeps a bigger share of the trading fees.

There’s real money at stake here. In Q3 2026, Coinbase’s prediction markets business was already on track to bring in over $200 million a year. If you think about it, this isn’t an overnight decision. In the run up to it all, Coinbase unveiled that it was buying prediction market startup The Clearing Firm in December 2025.

Then, in September this year, the CFTC gave the green light for its own clearing house.

Recent findings suggest that all that being mentioned, nothing’s set in stone. However, the pieces are clearly falling into place.

Crypto trading may have slowed down, but prediction markets have kept themselves out of the bleeding.

Since launch, revenue from the business has grown by 82% QoQ on average. In Q3 alone, daily traders went up by over 60%, compared to the quarter before.

Recent findings suggest that CFO Alesia Haas summed up the appeal pretty neatly. She said,.

Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility….

A substantial deal for an exchange that lives and dies by market cycles.

On the earnings call, Haas also mentioned that the upcoming clearing house would let Coinbase run its own contracts and earn more from them.

Worth pointing out, however, that Kalshi isn’t being cut out as partner contracts will stay on the platform.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota and Subaru’s latest electric SUVs are catching on with buyers, offering various options and prices ranging from about $35,000 to $45,000, or the “sweet spot” of the US market.

The US electric vehicle market rebounded in the third quarter with 262,649 EVs sold, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates, up 6.1% from Q2 and the strongest performance of the year.

Although nearly every automaker has sold fewer EVs so far this year than in the same period in 2025, as buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, a handful of brands are seeing considerably higher demand.

Outside of Rivian, Toyota and Subaru are the only brands that have higher year-over-year EV sales in the US through the third quarter.

Combined, Toyota and Subaru have sold nearly 50,000 EVs through the first nine months of 2026, more than double compared to the same period last year.

Toyota alone has sold nearly 35,000 electric vehicles, up 183.4% YOY, while Subaru sold 14,630, up 46.7%. And that’s not even including the additional 12,676 sold under the Lexus brand, up 137.4% YOY.

While the two Japanese automakers were infamously slow to transition to battery electric vehicles, the timing worked in their favor.

According to recent reports, after launching the heavily updated bZ in late 2025, previously called the bZ4X, Toyota’s electric SUV suddenly became one of America’s most popular EVs. Through Q3, it was the fourth best-selling EV in the US, trailing only the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.

Starting at $35,000, the Toyota bZ is one of the most affordable EVs in the US. It also offers up to 314 miles of range in the FWD Plus trim, which starts at $37,980.

Toyota and Subaru now each sell three electric SUVs, which share the same platform and technology.

With prices ranging from roughly $35,000 to about $45,000, Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, mentioned (via Bloomberg) Toyota and Subaru’s upcoming EVs are affordable and hit the “sweet spot” of the US car market.

Toyota also sells the smaller, sporty C-HR, starting at $37,080, and the larger, more rugged bZ Woodland, which starts at $45,380.

Subaru, on the other hand, sells the updated Solterra ($38,495, plus the smaller Uncharted ($34,995) and midsize Trailseeker ($39,995).

Karla Fisher, a Marine and retired engineer, told Bloomberg that the Subaru Trailseeker was her “most favorite car of all time.”.

While she considered buying an EV before the $7,500 federal credit expired last September, none met her requirements at the time. Fisher wanted at least 7″ of ground clearance, 250 miles or more range, and a price that was similar, or even less than a comparible gas-powered vehicle.

Industry observers note that the Subaru Trailseeker offers all of that and starts at under $40,000. Toyota and Subaru’s electric SUVs all start at about $45,000 or less, which is even less than the average fresh vehicle.

According to the latest Kelley Blue Book figures, the average price for a new vehicle in the US reached a record $51,109 in October, up 2.1% YOY.

Great as these may be, there is little inventory to be found.

There are less than 500 Uncharted available Nationwide.

You can't sell what you don't have. Yes, they can be ordered for sure, but how many missed sales does that model create?

According to recent reports, subaru spokesperson Dominick Infante mentioned the affordable EV prices are mainly thanks to its partnership with Toyota. “We do believe there’s an EV future,” Infante added.

Next year, both brands will add a three-row electric SUV with the Toyota Highlander EV and Subaru Getaway.

Thinking about making the switch to an EV? With the 2027 models at dealerships, now could be a good time to find a deal on current 2026 models. You can use the links below to see what’s available at Toyota and Subaru dealerships near you.

Latest Update: Best Hyperliquid trading bots: AI agents and bots compared

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it.
  • Recent findings suggest that most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet.
  • Many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it. They differ less in what they promise than in two practical questions: who decides the trades, and what the tool is allowed to do with your account. This guide compares the main Hyperliquid trading bots and AI trading agents in 2026, plus Hyperliquid’s vaults, against those questions. Each tool was compared on who decides the trades, what its key can do with your account, and what evidence of performance exists, using each provider’s own documentation in October 2026.

Recent findings suggest that most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet. The account owner approves a separate key that can sign orders for the account but cannot withdraw or transfer funds. These approvals expire, and approving a upcoming wallet under the same name replaces the old one. Some tools also recommend a sub-account, which keeps the bot’s balances and positions separate. The assets stay in the user’s own Hyperliquid account throughout, which is why most Hyperliquid bots can fairly be called non-custodial.

Many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order. It applies only after the user approves a maximum fee from the main wallet, and Hyperliquid caps it at 0.1% on perpetuals.

It has been revealed that tools are grouped by who supplies the trading logic: a managed model first, then signal execution, rule-based bots and open-source software (3Commas sits with the rule-based bots). Vaults come last because they replace a bot rather than run one. Hyperliquid’s own trading and funding fees apply to every option.

AlphaNet is built for Hyperliquid and supplies the trading logic itself. People pick one of its deep learning strategies for crypto perpetual futures and an allocation, and the model decides when to enter and exit each trade. It connects the way the exchange intends: the user approves an agent wallet that can place and cancel orders but cannot withdraw or transfer, and trades run from the user’s own account. Fresh deployments allow leverage up to 3× account equity. On cost, AlphaNet’s Hyperliquid trading bot charges no platform fee during the current promotional period, compared with builder fees of 0.035–0.1% per fill on several bots below; Hyperliquid’s protocol fees still apply, and a dynamic trading fee applies afterwards.

A newer group of AI agent projects on Hyperliquid connect language models to an API wallet and let them place trades. They are mostly early. In the first season of Alpha Arena, a short real-money competition on Hyperliquid, four of the six language models that took part finished with losses and two with gains.

Sources indicate that wunderTrading is built for traders whose strategy already exists as TradingView alerts or external signals. It turns those alerts into Hyperliquid orders and also offers DCA and grid bots, charging a 0.035% builder fee with no separate subscription.

goodcryptoX is a no-code app for grid, DCA, trailing, and TradingView bots on iOS, Android, and the web. Gainium covers similar bot types and adds backtesting and paper trading, with a choice between a free mode that adds a builder fee and paid aims that do not. Bitsgap brings its hosted grid and DCA bots to Hyperliquid alongside the centralised exchanges it already supports, and 3Commas, one of the most widely used bot platforms, lists Hyperliquid among its supported exchanges for spot and futures. With all of them, the bot executes your logic; the tool does not supply a trading edge.

Sources indicate that hummingbot has Hyperliquid spot and perpetual connectors and includes market-making scripts and arbitrage, TWAP, and grid executors. The self-run client charges no builder fee. It accepts either an API wallet or the main wallet’s private key; the second gives the software full control of the account, so the API wallet is the safer choice.

Industry observers note that rule-based bots have no platform-level record, because results depend on each user’s settings. Vaults are the most transparent option: every vault’s history is on-chain and visible in Hyperliquid’s app. Managed strategy platforms sit in between. AlphaNet publishes a running record of each strategy since its start date, and because trades run from owners’ own accounts, each user’s fills are on-chain and can be checked against it.

Instead of connecting a tool to your own account, you deposit into a vault that a leader trades. The protocol’s own vault, HLP, provides liquidity, performs liquidations, and earns a share of fees. User-run vaults follow individual strategies. Leaders take 10% of profits and must keep at least 5% of the vault, and deposits are locked for one day (four days for HLP).

Sources indicate that the choice comes down to the two questions this guide started with. First, decide who you want making the trades: your own rules, a signal you already trust, a trained model, or a vault leader. Then check what the tool is allowed to do with your account. On Hyperliquid, most tools need only an agent wallet that can trade but not withdraw, so there is rarely a reason to hand over a main wallet key or move funds into someone else’s control.

It has been revealed that two further checks are worth making before committing real capital. The first is cost per fill: builder fees on top of Hyperliquid’s own fees can add up. The second is the record: a vault’s history is on-chain, a managed strategy should publish a live one, and a rule-based bot has none until you build your own.

  • Hyundai unveiled its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the fresh IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai’s US electric vehicle lineup will look a bit different in 2027, including the latest IONIQ 6 N, a new range-topping IONIQ 9 trim, and a handful of minor updates to the IONIQ 5.

Hyundai unveiled its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the fresh IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.

While Hyundai discontinued the standard IONIQ 6, it added the high-performance IONIQ 6 N for the 2027 lineup.

According to recent reports, the IONIQ 6 N is Hyundai’s second performance EV, following the IONIQ 5 N. Powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, the electric sports car delivers a combined 641 hp and 568 lb-ft of torque.

Hyundai said the IONIQ 6 N can sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds, beating the IONIQ 5 N at 3.25 seconds.

Like the IONIQ 5 N, it also includes fun added features, like N e-Shift and an N Active Sound+ system that simulates the sounds and sensations of a traditional gas-powered sports car with an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission.

It uses an 84 kWh battery that provides up to 245 miles of pure electric driving range. Thanks to its 800V ultra-fast charging architecture, the IONIQ 6 N can charge from 10% to 80% in about 18 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Like Hyundai’s other electric vehicles, it comes standard with a native NACS charging port and a CCS adapter.

The 2027 IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are mostly carryover models with a few minor changes, while the IONIQ 5 N remains the same as the 2026 model year.

Changes to the IONIQ 5 for the 2027 model year include roof rails, which are now available on the SEL trim and above; previously, they were only available on the XRT and Limited trims.

Hyundai HomeLink will be available exclusively on the Limited trim, rather than SEL and above, in the current 2026 model year, while the Cargo Cover will be offered as an Accessory only.

Regarding color options, the Gravity Gold Matte and Sage Silver Matte will no longer be available for the 2027 IONIQ 5.

The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250, making it one of the most affordable EVs in the US.

Sources indicate that that’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. The extended-range SE RWD model is $2,500 more, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row SUV also received a handful of updates. The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 9 will be available with a latest Calligraphy Black Ink trim, while the Calligraphy Design will no longer be offered.

In a recent development, the 2027 IONIQ 9 Calligraphy and Calligraphy Black Ink trims gain a Virtual Gear Shift and heated third-row seats. All variants also gain a Tailgate Emergency Lamp.

According to recent reports, on the one hand... the Ioniq5 is due for an upgrade. On the other... I still absolutely love the way it looks, and notice just about every one I pass on the road.

It has been revealed that hyundai has yet to announce prices for the 2027 model. The base 2026 IONIQ 9 S starts at $58,995 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 335 miles.

The previous top-spec Performance Calligraphy Design AWD started at $76,490, so you can expect the latest Calligraphy Black Ink to be around the same, if not even more.

Bitcoin fell to a fresh bear market low as widespread selling picked up across crypto, stocks and gold.

Recent findings suggest that the Bitcoin sell-off deepened on Saturday, with the price reaching a low of $55,130, its lowest level since September 2024, extending a brutal run for risk assets. The latest sell-off deepens a bear market that began after Bitcoin peaked above $126,000 in October 2025.

Industry observers note that in an X post, Fidelity Investments' Director of Global Macro, Jurrien Timmer, says he remains bullish on Bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math. Timmer isn't oblivious to Bitcoin's recent poor performance, which he highlighted in a separate X post.

Sources indicate that "I would be remiss if I didn’t mention Bitcoin and its very poor price action. It has gotten significantly more correlated to the S&P 500 in recent weeks, trading more like a speculative risk asset than a monetary asset," Timmer wrote.

In a recent development, timmer added that Bitcoin has a dual personality in his own view, consisting of a monetary factor and a speculative factor. He depicted this by showing the rate of change in the GS non-profitable tech basket and the global money supply. When both are expanding rapidly, Bitcoin moons, and vice versa. Right now, risk appetites are receding as the AI theme corrects, while global liquidity is also receding, Timmer explained.

In his post, Timmer pointed out that Bitcoin is back on the Power Law support curve, which he indicates is a 'bit disheartening.' He highlighted the significance of this, saying that if Bitcoin’s price were ever to fall well below this support line, which is currently at $62,000 and rising, it would put his entire framework in doubt. "Never a dull moment!" he added.

In a recent development, I remain bullish on Bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math, but it’s a bit disheartening that we are back again sitting on that power law support curve. If Bitcoin’s price were to ever fall well below this support line (currently at $62k and rising), it would put my entire framework in doubt. Never a dull moment!

Timmer's viewpoint seems to align with that of veteran trader Peter Brandt, who noted that Bitcoin might have entered a "dicey" price range owing to its recent drop. "The territory below this level gets very dicey," he remarked, underlining the $57,803 price point for Bitcoin.

In September 2026, Timmer pointed to a potential double-bottom formation near $60,000, noting that breaking past resistance near $80,000–$86,000 would support a push toward $100,000. Timmer also projects Bitcoin could reach $300,000 by 2029 based on a power-law model.

Bitcoin now trades well below $62,000, and this raises the question of whether the framework underpinning Timmer’s outlook still holds.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, Binance is witnessing a rapid surge in its futures trading activity as the broader crypto market continues to face increased selling pressure.
  • While the market is still struggling with volatility and rapidly declining investor interest, the latest on-chain data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant indicates that futures traders have become extremely active on Binance.
  • The data highlights that both Bitcoin and Ethereum have seen their perpetual futures trading volume on Binance surge to a combined high of $39.8 billion as of November 20.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, Binance is witnessing a rapid surge in its futures trading activity as the broader crypto market continues to face increased selling pressure.

While the market is still struggling with volatility and rapidly declining investor interest, the latest on-chain data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant indicates that futures traders have become extremely active on Binance.

The data highlights that both Bitcoin and Ethereum have seen their perpetual futures trading volume on Binance surge to a combined high of $39.8 billion as of November 20.

Notably, this marks the highest level the metric has reached since September 21, indicating that traders are actively adjusting their positions to hedge against further losses as volatility continues to intensify.

Nonetheless, Bitcoin saw the highest increase in perpetual futures volume as it surged to $24.75 billion on the same day.

The data further demonstrated that the volume was slightly higher than the $24.57 billion recorded on September 21, when Bitcoin was trading above $87,000.

Ethereum, on the other hand, followed with a notable increase in the same metric, recording $15.05 billion in perpetual futures volume on the same day.

However, Ethereum did not entirely mimic Bitcoin in the trend as this was still below the $17.27 billion recorded during the September 21 trading period.

Further data shows that the high futures trading activity recorded on Binance on November 20 has coincided with BlackRock’s record Bitcoin ETF outflow.

The data shows that BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $511 million in net outflows on that day, marking a sharp reversal from the positive inflows seen in September.

While this shows that investors are also pulling their funds from Bitcoin ETFs, it marked the highest single-day outflow BlackRock has ever recorded.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Solana’s core developer, Anza, has unveiled its 2027 roadmap.
  • Recent findings suggest that structurally, the roadmap focuses on making Solana faster, more efficient, and capable of handling more activity.
  • It also prepares to increase the number of accounts supported in each transaction from 64 to 96 and make it easier to run models fully on-chain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solana’s core developer, Anza, has unveiled its 2027 roadmap.

Recent findings suggest that structurally, the roadmap focuses on making Solana faster, more efficient, and capable of handling more activity. The network aims to double its compute capacity and cut the compute units needed for token account transactions by 80%.

It also prepares to increase the number of accounts supported in each transaction from 64 to 96 and make it easier to run models fully on-chain.

Naturally, the question becomes whether Solana is preparing for its next growth phase. Interestingly, the previous major network upgrade was also performed by Anza.

This upgrade, called Alpenglow, brought down Solana’s finality time to 150ms from 12.8 seconds, making the network significantly faster.

The result? As the chart above reveals, Solana processed over 10 billion transactions in October, keeping monthly activity above that level. However, more than halfway through November, the network has recorded just over 2 billion transactions.

That’s 5x lower than October’s total, suggesting that the recent spike in activity may be losing steam. Given this, it might be too early to expect any bull run in 2027.

In fact, SOL is right now down 20% in October, which indicates that the market hasn’t seen increased demand from improving fundamentals just yet.

So, what does it say about the recent “Anthropic-driven” momentum on Solana [SOL]?

SPCX was first to demonstrate how major IPOs can bring fresh trading activity to Solana.

The launch of SpaceX’s tokenized stock, SPCX, on Solana on the 12th of June brought significant activity to the network.

The token recorded $108 million in 24-hour on-chain trading volume shortly after launch and crossed 10,000 holders within six days, with cumulative trading volume exceeding $350 million.

Recent findings suggest that notably, a similar trend has emerged following the ANT IPO launch. As the chart below shows, Anthropic’s ANT has generated over $29 million in trading volume on Solana since launch across three issuers. Backpack’s token alone accounted for $26.8 million, or nearly 92% of the total.

This shows how major IPO rolls out are bringing fresh trading activity to Solana.

Adding to this, DeFiLlama data reveals that Solana’s stablecoin market cap has risen nearly 3% in the past 24 hours, pointing to a fresh liquidity inflow after months of weakness.

However, the bigger picture remains mixed.

Industry observers note that despite the rise in on-chain activity and liquidity, SOL is still trading around $70. This suggests that the recent activity has yet to translate into stronger buying pressure.

For Solana’s 2027 roadmap to support a longer-term recovery, the network will therefore need to sustain this growth beyond short-term activity.

Anza’s 2027 roadmap aims to improve Solana’s speed, capacity, and overall network efficiency.

SPCX and ANT have boosted on-chain trading activity, but SOL’s price weakness suggests that stronger demand is still missing.

Breaking: Tesla confirms rare fresh delivery of 50 Semi electric trucks in Chicago

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has confirmed a latest batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.
  • Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its new Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.
  • The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, shows four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has confirmed a latest batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.

It’s a rare data point. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its new Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.

The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, shows four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.

Hello Windy CityChicago’s first 50 Semis en route for delivery pic.twitter.com/75kig8yWsb.

But the only 50-truck Semi order tied to Chicago belongs to HMD Trucking. The family-owned carrier was founded in Chicago in 1998, runs more than 650 trucks (almost all diesel), and ordered 50 Semis right after Tesla’s production event in September.

According to recent reports, HMD took its first truck on November 2 and indicates it’s the first Tesla Semi registered in Illinois. COO Michael Mahler mentioned Tesla “has been transparent with us regarding the capabilities of Semi every step of the way.”.

Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer ran a Semi for more than 4,000 miles over the summer and averaged 1.74 kWh per mile, right in line with Tesla’s 1.7 kWh/mile claim. The first trucks will mostly handle local runs around Chicago, and HMD is installing its own chargers there since Tesla’s Megacharger network is still concentrated along the I-5 and I-10 corridors in the West.

Industry observers note that owner Henry Malukas told MotorTrend the deal is worth about $15 million. That’s roughly $300,000 per truck, in line with the ~$290,000 Long Range pricing we reported when the first truck came off the high-volume line and a long way from the $180,000 Tesla advertised in 2017.

Here’s the problem: it’s nearly impossible to tell how many Semis Tesla is actually building.

Tesla launched volume production at its Sparks, Nevada factory on September 24, after pushing the ramp out of 2025. It says the 1.8 million sq ft plant is built for 50,000 trucks a year. But it never gave a ramp schedule, and its quarterly production and delivery reports only count “passenger vehicles sold to customers.” The Semi isn’t in there.

According to recent reports, so we’re left with proxies. Tesla notes its Semi fleet has over 98% uptime, without saying how major that fleet is. Before this year, the largest Semi fleet was PepsiCo’s, at 86 trucks in 2024. California’s truck voucher program received 965 Semi applications between January 2025 and February 2026, which points to real demand but says nothing about output.

The order book is the other clue. Einride ordered 500 Semis in August, WattEV has 370 on order, IMC Logistics wants 50 for California, and the ZET SCALE alliance picked Tesla as main supplier for 2,500 trucks. And now HMD’s 50 are rolling into Chicago, one of the first Semi fleets that will have to deal with a Midwest winter. Wisconsin’s Paper Transport has also been piloting a Semi in the Chicago market since the summer.

None of that adds up to a production rate, but it does look like Tesla is slowly ramping up deliveries.

Tesla keeps the Semi numbers vague on purpose. It’s happy to talk about a 50,000-truck-a-year factory, and it posts hero shots when a batch ships, but it won’t give the one number that indicates whether the factory is anywhere close to that.

I think the semi is going to be a big seller but its going to take some time to produce enough of them and for companies to gather enough data. Once the investment is justified, there will be customers and repeat customers. After that, it will only be a matter of time before other electric semi truck manufacturers start popping up with offerings and thats a good thing for everyone.

Industry observers note that the 50,000 figure is what makes the Semi look like a real business to investors instead of a niche program that took nine years to get going. Tesla has a long history of quoting capacity long before it reaches it, so we shouldn’t treat “built for 50,000” as anything more than a ceiling.

It has been revealed that our read: Tesla is still far from that 50,000 rate. Fifty trucks for one customer is 0.1% of a year at full capacity, and if Tesla were shipping in large volumes, a single 50-unit batch wouldn’t get its own post. But the ramp has clearly started, the order book is real, and it’s plausible Tesla gets into the thousands by the end of the year.

In a recent development, good for HMD, too. A 650-truck diesel fleet in a cold market is exactly the kind of customer the Semi has to win. Malukas admitted “we don’t have real numbers yet” on savings, and HMD’s own blog is fairly sober about cost and winter range. Local routes, depot charging and a Chicago winter is the right way to find out. It all sounds plausible for the Tesla Semi.

If you’re running an EV, powering it with home solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Ripple ETF Investors Hold On, But XRP Buyers Go Missing.

XRP ETF assets fell 31.6% despite modest redemptions, suggesting a lack of fresh demand, not a buyer exodus.

In a recent development, ripple’s XRP-linked ETF assets fell 31.6% from September 30 through the Friday cited in the video, compared with a 20.2% decline for Bitcoin funds. Yet redemptions remained modest.

Dana Love, PhD, a popular market analyst examining ETF flows and corporate filings, argues that missing buyers, not an investor stampede, help explain the XRP’s deeper slide this month.

The XRP coin traded at $0.967 this Friday morning, following a last Friday low of $0.89.

Dana Love’s central claim: Bitcoin-related selling is weighing on XRP, while demand from XRP funds and a closely watched treasury organization has failed to provide much support.

According to the figures presented, cumulative net inflows into XRP ETFs slipped from $1.809 billion on October 29 to $1.789 billion on Monday. That leaves roughly 98.9% of cumulative net inflows intact, despite the sharp decline in fund assets.

Industry observers note that but November through that Monday brought no positive daily net flows. “Nobody is running for the exits,” the analyst says, “but nobody newly introduced was walking in.”.

Bitcoin ETFs, meanwhile, recorded roughly $2.34 billion in November outflows through the same period. Monday’s $8 million inflow interrupted the selling, although the analyst cautions that one positive session does not establish a reversal.

The distinction matters: limited XRP ETF redemptions do not establish that XRP holders across the entire market are refusing to sell. Nor does a decline in fund assets measure withdrawals alone; falling token prices also reduce those balances.

Dana Love also questions Evernorth, the XRP treasury company whose October 14 release said it would “accumulate and deploy” XRP into institutional strategies beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The video estimates that Evernorth had about $111 million in cash, including subsequent warrant proceeds, and says its shares still traded above estimated underlying asset value.

That could support further fundraising, although the tech giant had not declared additional purchases in the period discussed.

It has been revealed that silence is not proof of inactivity. The analyst explicitly acknowledges that Evernorth may be buying without announcing every transaction.

For investors, the useful distinction is between broader market relief and renewed XRP-specific market demand.

Sustained Bitcoin ETF inflows would suggest selling pressure is easing; XRP inflows arriving independently, or a disclosed Evernorth purchase, would offer stronger evidence that XRP has found buyers of its own.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin reportedly became available at a massive discount on Kraken after a sharp dislocation in Kraken's dollar trading markets.
  • People reported being able to purchase BTC for as little as 24,250 CAD, equivalent to $16,900 at that time.
  • Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some people claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin reportedly became available at a massive discount on Kraken after a sharp dislocation in Kraken's dollar trading markets.

People reported being able to purchase BTC for as little as 24,250 CAD, equivalent to $16,900 at that time.

Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some people claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.

The cause the glitch is still unclear, while the reported transactions are yet to be verified.

The incident might have involved thin liquidity problem in Kraken's CAD order books.

Large sell orders reportedly overwhelmed available buy orders, leaving insufficient demand to absorb the selling pressure.

According to some accounts, at one point about 20 BTC was being sold every 15 minutes, causing the imbalance to push BTC price against CAD further down.

Sources indicate that one such transaction resulted in BTC price at around C$24,250, or $16,900. Compared with Bitcoin trading between $57,000-$58,000, the discount amounted to a staggering 71%. Other users reported BTC briefly trading around $27,000.

Sources indicate that kraken's status page continued to show its systems as operational during the incident. No official explanation from the exchange was available at the time of writing.

The reported dislocation highlights the risks associated with trading in markets with limited liquidity. When an order book lacks sufficient buy-side depth, even relatively large sell orders can cause prices to move sharply away from the broader market.

It has been revealed that on Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

According to recent reports, liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20.

According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

Industry observers note that bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions. Ethereum (ETH) fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations.

Binance accounted for 45.8% of all liquidations, and the largest single order was also on Binance: an $11.98 million ETH/USDT long position that was liquidated at $1,638.78.

💡 Key Takeaways
